claims.claim: At temperature 0, an LLM produced 80 unique completions over 1000 runs, and with batch-invariant kernels all 1000 were identical; the cause is that load, and thus batch size, varies nondeterministically.
Batch-invariant kernels cost roughly 2x (55 seconds versus 26 seconds), narrowing to 1.6x with improved attention kernels (42 seconds).

LLM-42 decodes with a non-deterministic fast path and enforces determinism via a lightweight verify-rollback loop, reusing existing kernels and incurring overhead only in proportion to the traffic that requires determinism.

À température 0, un LLM a produit 80 complétions uniques sur 1000 exécutions, et avec des noyaux invariants au batch les 1000 étaient identiques ; la cause est que la charge, et donc la taille de batch, varie de façon non déterministe.
Les noyaux invariants au batch coûtent environ 2x (55 secondes contre 26 secondes), réduit à 1,6x avec des noyaux d'attention améliorés (42 secondes).

LLM-42 décode avec un chemin rapide non déterministe et impose le déterminisme via une boucle légère de vérification et rollback, réutilisant les noyaux existants et n'encourant un surcoût qu'en proportion du trafic qui requiert le déterminisme.

sources.label: Thinking Machines Lab: Defeating Nondeterminism in LLM Inference
sources.excerpt: even when we adjust the temperature down to 0 (thus making the sampling theoretically deterministic), LLM APIs are still not deterministic in practice ... the primary reason nearly all LLM inference endpoints are nondeterministic is that the load (and thus batch-size) nondeterministically varies ... With batch-invariant kernels enabled, all of our 1000 completions are identical [versus 80 unique completions unoptimized] ... approximately 2x slower (55 seconds vs. 26 seconds), reducing to 1.6x slowdown with improved attention kernels (42 seconds).

sources.label: LLM-42: Enabling Determinism in LLM Inference with Verified Speculation (arXiv 2601.17768)
sources.excerpt: the same prompt may yield different outputs across different runs. At the system level, this non-determinism arises from floating-point non-associativity combined with dynamic batching ... LLM-42 decodes tokens using a non-deterministic fast path and enforces determinism via a lightweight verify-rollback loop ... LLM-42 mostly re-uses existing kernels unchanged and incurs overhead only in proportion to the traffic that requires determinism.
